reviews.lessons: WideOpen has zero trades — it has never been validated in live conditions, so loosening every filter simultaneously (phase_confidence, R:R, RSI band, ATR band, trend filter) is a leap of faith with no empirical grounding. The 'any-of' tier now accepts six different conditions, meaning almost any stock that isn't in confirmed markdown or RSI>78 can qualify, which defeats the purpose of a filter stack. MTF interest at 0.04%/day means marginal setups — those that just barely clear a 1.3 R:R — will be eaten alive if the move takes 4-5 days to develop. The prior version (v2, presumably) was tightened for a reason; relaxing everything at once without trade data to justify each relaxation is strategy drift, not refinement. A strategy with no trades is not a 'wide open' opportunity — it is an untested system masquerading as one.
reviews.changes: 1) RESTORE phase_confidence to 0.45 — 0.35 is below the level where Wyckoff phase identification carries any reliable signal. 2) RESTORE R:R to 1.6 minimum — at 1.3 with MTF costs the edge is essentially zero on slow moves; 1.6 gives a real buffer. 3) TIGHTEN the any-of tier: require AT LEAST TWO of the six conditions to be true rather than any one — this restores meaningful filtration without being as strict as requiring all. 4) NARROW RSI band back to 40-72 — entries at RSI 35-40 are bottom-fishing without Wyckoff spring confirmation, and entries at 72-78 are momentum chasing near resistance; neither suits a 5-day MTF swing. 5) DIAGNOSE the zero-trade issue at source: check whether the signal scanner is actually running and producing candidates before concluding filters are too tight — if no candidates are being scored, loosening thresholds does nothing. 6) When live trades begin, log entry reason codes so future reviews can distinguish MAX_HOLD_5D losers from STOP losers — without that, the next review will be equally blind.

reviews.lessons: Wyckoff_v3_WideOpen has zero closed trades, so there is no empirical loss pattern to diagnose — every parameter relaxation (phase_confidence 0.35, R:R 1.3, RSI 35-78, ATR 0.7-8.0, the broad 'any-of' tier now satisfied by above_50dma alone) was made in a vacuum without trade evidence to justify it. The 'any-of' block is now so permissive that almost any liquid large-cap on an up-day qualifies, which is not a Wyckoff filter — it is noise dressed as a system. R:R of 1.3 is barely above breakeven once MTF interest (~0.2% over 5 days) plus round-trip friction (~0.1-0.15%) are deducted; at that threshold a winning trade needs to move fast or the economics collapse. Lowering phase_confidence to 0.35 means the system will frequently enter in ambiguous Wyckoff phases where accumulation vs. distribution is unresolved — exactly the kind of chop that produces MAX_HOLD_5D exits and interest bleed.
reviews.changes: Start fresh with a tighter, evidence-grounded ruleset before live deployment: (1) Restore phase_confidence >= 0.45 — below this threshold Wyckoff phase is a coin-flip and the label adds no information. (2) Require R:R >= 1.8 to nearest hard resistance/support — after 0.4-0.5% round-trip+interest friction this still delivers a net positive expectancy on a 40% hit rate. (3) Reinstate volume_confirming AND (wyckoff_phase_score >= 1.0 OR == 0.5) as hard 'all' conditions, not optional 'any-of' — volume is the only Wyckoff confirmation signal available without fundamentals. (4) Drop above_50dma from the any-of tier entirely; it overlaps with trend_up and dilutes the filter. Keep above_200dma as the trend anchor. (5) Tighten ATR band to 1.0-5.0 — below 1% the stock cannot cover friction in 5 days; above 5% stop placement becomes uncontrollably wide and sizing is distorted. (6) Run the revised rules in paper simulation for at least 15-20 signals before live MTF deployment so the any loosening decisions are grounded in observed signal frequency and win-rate rather than parameter guessing.

reviews.lessons: No trades were executed under Wyckoff_v3_WideOpen, so there is zero empirical evidence to evaluate — no entries, no exits, no MTF drag, no stop behaviour. The strategy relaxed almost every filter from v2 (phase_confidence, R:R, RSI, ATR, trend filter) while keeping the same hard risk limits; without a trade sample we cannot tell whether the looser filters improve hit-rate or simply admit lower-quality setups. The 'any-of' tier now has six conditions, several of which are near-trivially satisfied in a trending market (above_50dma, trend_up), which risks rubber-stamping weak Wyckoff reads with a momentum proxy. MTF interest remains a structural headwind of ~0.4–0.5% per 5-day hold that requires a meaningful edge to overcome, and that edge is unproven here.
reviews.changes: 1) Run the strategy in paper-signal mode for at least 15 trading days before committing MTF capital, logging every signal that WOULD have triggered so you can inspect R:R, phase quality and outcome without paying interest on losers. 2) Tighten the any-of gate: require at LEAST TWO of the six any-of conditions to be true simultaneously (e.g. volume_confirming AND above_200dma, or wyckoff_phase_score>=1.0 AND trend_up) — a single easy condition should not be sufficient to clear the gate. 3) Restore R:R minimum to 1.6; at 1.3 the gross reward barely covers the 0.4–0.5% MTF + transaction cost floor on a 5-day hold without a buffer for slippage. 4) Keep phase_confidence at 0.35 but add a secondary check: if phase_confidence is between 0.35 and 0.44 (i.e. below the old threshold), require wyckoff_phase_score >= 1.0 to compensate — do not allow low-confidence phases to clear on any easy any-of condition alone. 5) Log every non-entry (signal seen but blocked) with the blocking reason; after 20 such observations re-examine which filters are over-blocking vs which are correctly filtering, then make data-driven adjustments rather than blanket relaxation.

reviews.lessons: WideOpen has zero trades, so there is no execution record to diagnose — every relaxation made since v1/v2 (lower phase_confidence, wider RSI band, looser ATR, softened trend filter) has produced a strategy that still fires nothing in live conditions. The 'any-of' tier is now so broad (six conditions, any one suffices) that it adds no real discriminating power, yet the 'all' tier's phase_confidence floor of 0.35 may still be blocking entries if the scoring model rarely crosses even that softened threshold. Without trades, MTF interest is not eating capital, but opportunity cost and strategy drift are the real concerns. Progressively loosening parameters without a live feedback loop risks masking a deeper model-calibration problem: the Wyckoff phase scorer itself may be the bottleneck, not the thresholds wrapped around it.
reviews.changes: Stop loosening thresholds blindly. First, run a diagnostic backfill: log the raw daily output of phase_confidence, wyckoff_phase_score, volume_confirming, and trend_up for every ticker in the universe over the past 60 sessions and find where the actual distribution sits — if phase_confidence is routinely 0.1-0.25, no threshold above that will fire. Second, replace the composite Wyckoff scorer with a simpler, directly observable entry rule that does not depend on a black-box confidence score: require (a) price within 1 ATR of a clearly defined support level identified by swing lows or volume-by-price nodes, (b) the last two candles show above-20-day-average volume, (c) RSI 38-65, (d) price above the 50-DMA, and (e) measured R:R to next resistance >= 1.5. These are all directly computable from OHLCV. Third, restore tighter ATR band (1.0-5.0) to avoid illiquid or hyper-volatile outliers that inflate spread cost. Fourth, paper-trade this simplified ruleset for two weeks with mandatory trade logging before any further parameter changes — no more version iterations without at least 10 closed trades of data.

reviews.lessons: Wyckoff_v3_WideOpen has zero closed trades, so there is no execution history to audit — no exit-reason breakdown, no stop-frequency, no MAX_HOLD_5D bleed, no MTF interest drag to measure. The v3 relaxations (phase_confidence 0.35, R:R 1.3, RSI 35-78, ATR 0.7-8.0, 50-DMA qualifying alone) are directionally worrying on paper: each individual loosening is modest but stacked together they substantially widen the funnel and risk letting in low-conviction, slow-moving setups that are exactly the ones MTF interest eats alive. The 'any-of' tier is now so broad (six conditions of which any one suffices) that a stock can enter with weak Wyckoff score, no volume confirmation, below the 200-DMA, and merely above the 50-DMA — that is not a swing setup, that is noise. Without a live track record we cannot confirm the harm, but the architecture creates the conditions for the two classic failure modes simultaneously: late entries on marginal setups (stop-outs) and low-momentum drift trades (MAX_HOLD_5D losses with interest drag).
reviews.changes: 1) Raise phase_confidence back to 0.40 minimum — 0.35 is below the threshold where Wyckoff phase calls carry tradeable signal. 2) Raise R:R floor to 1.5; at 1.3 the expected-value math barely survives round-trip costs plus five days of MTF interest. 3) Tighten the 'any-of' tier: require AT LEAST TWO of the six conditions to be true, not just one — this restores multi-confirmation logic without being as strict as v2. 4) Keep the 50-DMA qualifier but only if volume_confirming is also true; a stock above the 50-DMA alone with no volume is not a trend resumption candidate. 5) Narrow ATR band back to 1.0-6.0 on the low end — sub-1% ATR stocks cannot produce a meaningful swing within five sessions after costs. 6) Deploy the strategy on paper NOW with these tightened parameters to generate actual trade data; without closed trades this review is theoretical and the next review cycle will be the same.
